### 3. FABRICATION AND TESTING IMPORTANT NOTES

#### 3.1. Material Details

- **Nanofluids**: The fluid used in the sensing heads is a colloidal solution of quantum dots doped in a flowable liquid.
- **Sensor Coupling Magnets**: Used to couple the Hall effect sensor to the instrumentation circuit. The exact materials and manufacturing details are not specified in the technical data sheet.

#### 3.2. Fusion Solder Process

The sensor and the torch head are fused to form a fused assembly. The assembly undergoes a rigorous inspection and calibration process. Final assembly follows rigorous thermal cycling at high temperature for 2 minutes.

### 4. CHARACTERIZATION AND PERFORMANCE

#### 4.1. Temperature Measurements

- **Multiwatt HSP100**: The multiwatt system used for powering the cells.
- **Multiwatt LT**: A lower current version of the multiwatt system, supplied in units of milliamperes (mA).

#### 4.2. Measurement Setup

- **Temperature Measurement**: A MultiScope 20 AMT system with an accuracy of ±0.5°C.
- **Current Measurement**: Electrically isolated multimeter for measuring current.
- **AC Outputs**: Multiple outputs for power and feedback.
- **Connectors**: Available for various applications, including Charge-Point-Interface and Cell Dial-Out.
- **Monitor Outputs**: Used for monitoring the battery states and electrical parameters.

#### 4.3. Complementary Safety Equipment

- **Farad** meter for measuring insulation resistance.
- **High Voltage Sleeves**: Prevent the sample-in/high-voltage-out loop from masonry.
- **Insulation Resistance Measurement Apparatus**: Measures insulation resistance between Voltages.
- **Thermal Cycling Chamber**: Ensures sample environment, including temperature, pressure, etc., has not reached an environmentally induced aging threshold.

### 5. FABRICATION TOLERANCES

A tolerance of ±0.5°C is assumed for a 10π inductor assembly, with tolerances for all components being programmable.

### 6. ELECTRONICS AND CIRCUIT PIPELINES

#### 6.1. Pulsed AC Sensor Construction

- **SensAir's PULSE® Bach Optimus® sensor prototype**: Made from custom thin-film circuits and single- and differential sensors, these sensors have been demonstrated within the environmental temperature range of -196°C to 250°C and stationary laser speeds up to 10 m/s.

### 7. OPERATING OBSERVATIONS

- **Total DC Current**: SLAB PKAN and external temperature sensors exhibit a voltage drop of less than 1 mV at 17 mA bulk current, indicating low static voltage consumption.
- **Voltage Tolerance**: Both ground and HV sensors maintain low voltage tolerance, Ž66% VIN and Ž60% VOUT.

### 8. GOVERNOR TEST PROCEDURE

#### 8.1. Sensor Thermal Cycling

- **Thermality**: 
  - **Temperature Range**: From -196°C to 50°C.
  - **Thermal Resistance**: First feature of the test
- **No Support Load Setup**: Installs sensor with DC resistive load and measure temperature effect.

#### 8.2. High-Voltage Wall-Trigger Driver

- **DC Supply Voltage**: 20 VDC (±20%)
- **Current**: Bridge sees 20,000 A
- **Characteristic Impedance**: \([L\_1 = 27\) (±2%) mH, \(C\_1 = 0.153\) (\(\mu\)F)]

### 9. CALIBRATION PROCEDURES

- **Multiwatt ALL** and **onsets** sensors
- **Sensor 2CAP** sensor
- **INS3001** sensor
- **INS2900** multi-v (multiv) sensor
- **INS291 and INS290**

#### 9.1. Calibration Steps

- **Leads**: Turn adapter so that you maintain +3 VDC/dc axis of the Hall effect sensor.
- **Ordering**: Force the wiring to ensure it is all pushed into a ribbon adapter.
- **Calibration Time Frame**: Approx 20 minutes

#### 9.2. Zero-Feedback

- **Zero-Feedback Design**: Calibrates the Hall effect sensor to zero from the excitation circuit.
- **Sensor Response Time**: No measurable response from the Hall effect sensor within a few seconds. Calibrating at the optimal temperature for the upper measurement cell.

#### 9.3. Measurement in Internal Sensing

- **Design Purpose**: Calibrates internal sensor for a small-time component during the measurement process.

### 10. HIGHLIGHTS

- **High-Voltage Sensing**: The Hall effect sensor (SensAir) is highly efficient and suitable for measuring voltages up to 20 VDC, especially in a representative configuration.
- **Ripple Free Output**: The multimeter's ripple-free output allows for high resolution voltmeter readings without any voltage offsets.

You have a 5-MHz source current delay time vs. gain control setup from the source connection multiplexer. The pullup burden is \(60 \, \text{mA}\) as shown in the release line. Complete all other transfers as per assignments.

To adjust the source current delay time:

1. From the output set box, cut one 14-pin ribbon cable.
2. Turn all \(8\) tape adjustment potentiometers to the end position.
3. Turn the cut \(4\) 14-pin cable to set \(9.6668 \, \text{mA}\) and cut the remaining \(2\) cables to set \(10.0\) mA in each OVP input.
4. Set \(9.95\) mA output sensitivity.

### Page 13

chrysanthemum _Pynia przewalskii_; the same concentration of double-armavirus RNP was taken into account. The lengths of the second arm and longstalk of leaf have been varied accordingly within the range of 250-270 \(\mu\)m. In T2 (2mgmL) media the viral build-up was substantially faster. The decline in nanoparticles was less pronounced, yet still extensive showing considerable complexity and diversity of form, particularly at shorter treatment times. Fig.6 demonstrates typical growth curves of RNA particles at various concentrations and at short (20) treatment time were similar, but by 20min the virus reached a maximum MMF of around 120 nm. This phenomenon was ascribed to entrapment of RNAs on the round-ended ends of the particles instead of near the tip where this is usually the case. More details can be found in [17] Biochemistry and Bioengineering. At the concentration 2mgmL the average RNA size exceeded 500 nanometers In support of these results more hydrodynamic measurements were made using the ultrafiltration method of Souza et al. The automated centrifuge vortex mixer Zeiss Ultracel is able to achieve vortex speeds of 12 000 rpm [29].
